narrative_purpose: Shows why a zeitgeber is phase-dependent rather than a simple on-switch: the same blue light pulse delivered early or late in subjective night pushes an identical internal oscillator in opposite directions.
subject: Two matched sleeping human silhouettes shown in dark rooms with identical narrow blue light pulses reaching closed eyelids. In the left room, the subject is early in biological night: the molecular clock inside a translucent head is shown as a cyan protein cycle shifted toward a later position relative to a faint external dawn glow. In the right room, the subject is late in biological night: the same cycle is shifted toward an earlier position, closer to the coming dawn. A third small central vignette shows midday light striking an awake eye while the internal cycle remains unchanged.
scene: Three controlled chronobiology observation bays with identical beds, light sources and bodies; only the internal phase and the faint horizon outside differ.
camera: Matched side-on cutaway views through each dark room, with the translucent head and internal oscillator visible without medical gore.
light: The test pulse is narrow Pandora cyan in every bay; early-night background is deep indigo, late-night background has a pale pre-dawn rim, midday vignette is softly lit but subdued.
palette: Indigo rooms, cyan test light and oscillator, pale mist dawn, tiny amber horizon accent only in the late-night panel.
style: Painterly physiological comparison with quiet clinical clarity, not a chart and not science-fiction UI.
detail_level: Clear repeated light pulse, closed eye, internal cycle position and outside dawn cue; room detail remains minimal.
composition: Large early-night bay left, narrow midday dead-zone vignette center, large late-night bay right. Preserve dark margins beside each head for interface labels.
consistency_notes: Use the same subject and same blue pulse in both night panels. The only teaching difference is when the light arrives and whether the internal cycle shifts later or earlier.
negative_prompt: no text, no arrows, no readable clocks, no neon UI, no split personality, no medical horror, no photo or CGI look
